creative_direction.name: Flint Gallery Oblique
creative_direction.brief: A constructed mineral gallery: one monolithic cleft flint wall in cool bone-grey stone meets a continuous honed pale stone ground at a horizon aligned with the true base line, while a single crisp oblique shadow edge rakes the wall from upper left like late sun through a gallery slot. The cutout stands left of centre on that ground, contact shadow anchoring its foot, while the right wall stays calm for a wrapped Times column: brand at column head, the name across two tall serif lines, a short rust rule closing the column like a chisel mark. Vertical overlap with the shoulder but wide horizontal clearance keeps the two-column grid deliberate; cold split-stone matte against warm amber juice reads as earth under architecture.
creative_direction.material: cleft flint stone wall with honed pale stone ground
creative_direction.lighting: bright directional late-day light casting one crisp oblique shadow edge on the wall, warm ambient on the ground
